audit.title: Smart Value Recapture (SVR) Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The section leads are good ("Oracle Extractable Value (OEV) refers to a subset of MEV created during the transmission of oracle reports…"), but the top of the page opens with announcement banners (orderflow auctions, onboarding contact, Base/Arbitrum expansion) before the canonical SVR definition. An engine skimming the first chunk lifts news, not the definition.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis:
Strong — 15 headings, 1 H1, no level skips, sensible ~73-word median sections, a clean network→auction table. Weakness: raw JSX/HTML artifacts (`

` tags, `{" "}`, unrendered markdown links inside HTML) leak into the served content.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured 12 numerals, **0 with units**, plus vague quantifiers "many/most." "Configurable delay… can be set to any amount of seconds," "tens of billions in DeFi TVL," and an unquantified "standard rate" revenue split all beg for numbers.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 16 links but **0 to primary sources** — links go to blog posts, forms, and internal pages. No link to Flashbots MEV-Share spec, Aave docs, or an OEV primary reference.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. MEV and OEV both have crisp, liftable one-sentence definitions near first use. SVR's own definition is slightly more diffuse.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured: no JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/ dateModified, no og/twitter tags, inLanguage absent. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` — but no structured signals were served.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Critical. The only code block ("2. Read from the SVR Feed") is an **unclosed, empty** ```` ```solidity ```` fence (line 132) with no imports, no address, no interface call. The single actionable integration example is broken.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers what/why/how, variants, default activation, searcher paths, economics, risk. No troubleshooting/FAQ or error-string sections; no symptom-phrased headings.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Terminology is consistent (SVR, OEV, DON). Marred by rendering artifacts and an awkward "This delay can be set to any amount of seconds" / "This helps ensures" typo.

audit.summary:
This is a conceptually solid page explaining Chainlink SVR/OEV mechanics with clean section
structure and good canonical definitions of MEV and OEV. Its GEO ceiling is capped by three
concrete, fixable defects: a **broken/unclosed and empty Solidity code block** (line 132) that
leaves the only "how to integrate" snippet unusable, **zero structured metadata** (no JSON-LD,
canonical, or dates per the measured facts), and **vague quantitative claims** where numbers
would win citations (delay, revenue split, TVL). The prose is strong; the machine-facing layer
and code are not. Fixing the code block and adding specifics/metadata would move this from
Developing to Strong.

recommendations.title: Fix the broken integration code block
recommendations.change: Insert a complete, closed snippet: SPDX + pragma, `import` of `AggregatorV3Interface`, a constructor taking the SVR aggregator address, a `latestRoundData()` read, and a comment noting "use the SVR-enabled feed address from the Feed Addresses page." Show expected return fields.
recommendations.why: The one agent-runnable artifact is currently unusable; a complete snippet is the highest-value single fix for coding agents and for code-block retrieval.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with concrete numbers
recommendations.where: Fail-Safe Fallback; Economics and Revenue Split; "Proven Oracle Infrastructure"
recommendations.issue: "can be set to any amount of seconds," "split… at a standard rate," "tens of billions."
recommendations.change: State the actual default/typical delay in seconds, the actual recapture split percentages (or a range), and cite a dated TVL figure. Numbers with units are among the highest-lift GEO changes.
recommendations.why: Measured 0 numerals with units; quantitative claims are what engines quote when answering "how long is the SVR delay" or "what's the SVR revenue split."

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical, and last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-trust and E-E-A-T; absent dates weaken this fast-moving page (multiple network-expansion banners) on freshness.

recommendations.title: Lead with the canonical definition, demote banners
recommendations.issue: Announcement paragraphs precede the SVR definition.
recommendations.change: Move the "Chainlink SVR Feeds introduce a novel and secure way to recapture OEV…" sentence to the first liftable line; collapse the orderflow/onboarding banners into a callout below it.
recommendations.why: The first chunk should answer "what is SVR," not surface time-bound news.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: No sections phrased as user questions ("How do I read an SVR feed?", "What is the SVR fallback delay?", "How is SVR revenue split?").
recommendations.change: Add a short FAQ with these exact questions as H3s, each answered in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by question and symptom; question-titled sections win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add primary-source citations
recommendations.change: Link "Flashbots MEV-Share" to the Flashbots docs and "Aave" to Aave's docs on first mention.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Clean rendering artifacts and typos
recommendations.issue:
Raw `

`, `{" "}`, unrendered `[subscribe here](…)` inside HTML; "This helps ensures."
recommendations.change: Convert JSX/HTML blocks to clean markdown; fix the grammar.
recommendations.why: Clean, fluent presentation is independently rewarded and prevents garbled lifts.

antiPatterns: **Broken code fence** — unclosed, empty Solidity block (line 132); no imports/config.
**Rendering leakage** — raw HTML/JSX and unrendered markdown links in served content.
**Undated content** on a page carrying multiple time-sensitive network-expansion banners.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced on-page — good; verify it lists this URL and the searcher-onboarding children for canonical-hub discoverability.
Site-level: ensure `TechArticle` schema and canonical tags are templated across data-feeds docs, not just here.
CLI should pass raw `<head>` on the next run — head metadata could not be verified, so metadata scoring reflects served-body absence only.
